subject: Intermittent API failures -> transit-gateway route shadowing / on-prem return-path
messages:
From: Ashley Jones <ashley.jones@acme.com>
Date: 2026-09-12T08:14:00-07:00
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@acme.com>, ACME SRE <sre@acme.com>
Subject: Intermittent failures to private deployment (US-west)

Hi Dylan,

We started seeing intermittent 504s from our service-to-service calls that target the Redwood private deployment in our VPC (us-west-2). Failures are short (30-90s) and then recover; no obvious changes on our side.

Attached is a pcap taken at our NAT gateway and a screenshot of the transit-gateway route table when this was happening. Traceroute shows packets leaving our subnet, hitting the TGW, then next hop appears to be unreachable.

Can you take a look from the Redwood side? We are on the private deployment (customer id: ACME-1192) using your Transit-GW integration and static routes to on-prem.

Thanks,
Ashley
Ashley Jones
SRE Lead, ACME Industries

Attachments: acme-trace-20260912.pcap, tgw-route-table-20260912.png

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-12T08:41:00-07:00
To: Ashley Jones <ashley.jones@acme.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Subject: Re: Intermittent failures to private deployment (US-west)

Thanks Ashley — looping in Marissa (network infra) and Dev (private deploy SE) to help triage.

Quick ask while we dig:
- Can you confirm whether the failures correlate with any TGW route changes or route propagation events on your side?
- If possible, paste a short output of `ip route` from the instance that saw the 504 and the VPC route table for the subnet.

We will pull logs from the Redwood customer-facing vSR/vrouter and check for asymmetric return-paths or blackhole routes.

I'll report back within 1 hour.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-12T09:12:00-07:00
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Subject: Re: Intermittent failures to private deployment (US-west)

Following up — I pulled the vSR routing logs and saw repeated BGP withdraws for the route announced by ACME's TGW at 08:09:12 UTC and then a flurry of static-route re-ads (our controller was pushing a high-priority static route). Observed symptoms:

- Traffic from ACME -> Redwood nodes is being accepted; return traffic occasionally follows a different path into a shared peering VPC where there is a more specific route with higher priority (shadowing their intended static route).
- When the peer VPC holds that more-specific route, our vrouter drops the return packets due to RPF/security checks.

I suspect "route shadowing" combined with AWS route priority and a leftover blackhole entry in the on-prem router is causing brief blackholes.

Next steps I'm doing now:
- Confirm exact route priorities and timestamps (already captured).
- Pull agent logs from the affected instance group and check NAT port exhaustion counters.

Adding logs and route snapshots to JIRA NET-4319.

-Marissa
Network Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@acme.com>
Date: 2026-09-12T10:03:00-07:00
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai, ACME SRE <sre@acme.com>
Subject: Re: Intermittent failures to private deployment (US-west)

Thanks Marissa. I can confirm we saw a maintenance event on our edge router at 08:08 UTC which briefly withdrew the TGW announcement while our ops pushed a static route cleanup. We also saw concurrent automated route injection from a partner peering (partner-vpc) that advertised a /24 specific that overlapped ACME's /16.

We will remove the overlapping advertisement and lock down route propagation. In the meantime, is there a mitigation we can apply on the Redwood side to avoid the short blackholes — perhaps configuring an automatic fallback route or relaxing strict RPF checks for this customer subnet for a short window?

-Sanjay
Senior Network Engineer, ACME

From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-12T13:20:00-07:00
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Subject: Re: Intermittent failures to private deployment (US-west)

We tested two mitigations in a canary:
1) Temporarily add a lower-priority /32 host route for the affected ACME nodes in the vSR so the return path prefers the on-prem tunnel even if a more-specific /24 is advertised elsewhere.
2) Add an exception to the RPF/strict-source-check for ACME's prefix on the vSR for 1 hour to allow symmetric traffic to be accepted while propagation events settle.

Result: (canary run) — 20 minutes without a 504 on the canary host, normal traffic resumed. NAT port counters did not spike.

I recommend we:
- Apply the RPF relax + /32 host route for the affected CIDR for 60 minutes across the cluster, monitor, then rollback.
- Ask ACME to remove the partner /24 advertisement and confirm TGW route propagation stability.

I'll prepare a short runbook for ops to apply the temporary controls (see attached redwood-agent-logs-09-12.tar.gz).

—Dev
Platform SE, Redwood Private Deployments

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-13T16:47:00-07:00
To: Ashley Jones <ashley.jones@acme.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@acme.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Subject: Re: Intermittent failures to private deployment (US-west)

Hi Ashley / Sanjay — final update from Redwood side:

Actions taken (Redwood):
- Applied temporary /32 host route + RPF relax for ACME prefix across the affected vSR cluster at 2026-09-12T14:10:00Z.
- Monitored for 24 hours; no further 504 spikes observed during propagation window.
- Reverted temporary relax at 2026-09-13T14:05:00Z after ACME confirmed partner route was removed and TGW announcements stabilized.

Root cause summary:
- Overlapping more-specific route from a partner VPC was being propagated into the network during a maintenance event, and due to AWS route selection priority the shared peering path temporarily won, causing return traffic to be routed into a path not expecting ACME traffic. Strict RPF on our vSR dropped those return packets (brief blackhole).

Permanent recommendations:
- ACME: Enforce route filtering on partner peering to prevent accidental /24 advert into TGW.
- Redwood: We will add an automated detection rule for cluster-wide BGP withdraw flurries tied to customer prefixes and a safe default fallback route that can be applied automatically for short windows. This will ship as an infra guard in the next sprint.

Please reply if you want the short runbook we used to apply the temporary controls and the exact commands.

Thanks again for the quick coordination — Jonas from our network reliability group will follow up with a change to detect this class of failure automatically.

Best,
Dylan
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
